title: Hiring Process Steps From Opening a Role to Onboarding a Hire Oct 2026
summary: See how a 7-step hiring process gives founders clear owners and decision criteria at every stage. October 2026.
body_markdown:
You’ve picked a finalist, but compensation approval is still pending and nobody has planned their first week. Getting to a yes leaves work unfinished when the hiring process stops at interviews. Seven[hiring process steps](https://www.dover.com/) connect the full search, from approving the role to preparing the new hire, with named owners and clear handoffs, so once those owners have authority to act, fewer decisions may fall back on you.


**TLDR:**


-


Use 7 hiring steps: approve, define, source, screen, interview, offer, and onboard.


-


Give each stage an owner and decision criteria; assign each active candidate a next action.


-


Use consistent interview questions and independent scorecards before team discussion.


-


After interviews, review evidence, approve pay, send a written offer, and confirm acceptance.


-


Track time in stage, offer acceptance, and early hire outcomes to spot bottlenecks.


## The Hiring Process and Its Core Stages


The hiring process covers identifying a staffing need, selecting and hiring a candidate, onboarding, and reviewing results. Assigning owners and decision criteria to each stage can help founders avoid repeated interviews, inconsistent assessments, and stalled offer approvals.


This guide uses seven hiring process steps. Frameworks with four, five, eight, or fifteen steps group or separate similar activities. Government hiring procedures, including USPS, CBP, and TSA processes, fall outside this[recruitment process guide](https://www.dover.com/blog/recruitment-process-guide) ’s scope.


## Hiring Process Steps Flowchart and Template


Approve → Define → Source → Screen → Interview → Offer → Onboard


Step Owner Output Advance when


Approve Founder Budget Funded


Define Manager Brief Agreed


Source Recruiter Pool Reviewable


Screen Recruiter Shortlist Qualified


Interview Interviewers Scorecards Sufficient evidence


Offer Manager Offer Accepted


Onboard Manager Checklist Completed


-


Insufficient shortlist: resume sourcing.


-


Unqualified candidate: reject; continue screening.


-


Declined offer: revisit selection or sourcing.


Copy into Word, PowerPoint, or Excel; export as PDF.


## Step 1: Identify the Hiring Need and Approve the Budget


Tie the hire to a measurable business outcome. For replacements, reassess scope; for new roles, confirm workload warrants headcount. Consider internal moves or redistributing work first.


Budget for compensation, recruiting, and onboarding, including manager time. Without HR, the founder approves spending; the hiring manager checks capacity and defines success.


Record an approved hiring brief with:


-


Decision owner responsible for approval


-


Budget covering the full hiring cost


-


Target start window


-


Measurable role outcomes


## Step 2: Define the Role and Write the Job Description


Writing an effective[job description](https://www.dover.com/blog/job-description-guide) means translating the business need into observable work: “debugs production failures” gives reviewers more to assess than “strong technical skills.”


Your posting should include:


-


Responsibilities, with required skills separated from preferences


-


Reporting relationship and work arrangements


-


A realistic compensation range for the scope


-


Application instructions and interview stages


Create a role scorecard pairing each requirement with evidence to look for and a rating scale. Interviewers should reuse it to keep assessments consistent across hiring process steps.


## Step 3: Source and Attract Candidates


Choose[candidate sourcing techniques](https://www.dover.com/blog/candidate-sourcing-techniques-guide) based on the role:


-


Consider internal candidates seeking growth.


-


Ask employees for referrals from trusted networks.


-


Use relevant job boards for active applicants.


-


Join professional communities for specialized searches.


-


Try campus recruiting for entry-level roles.


-


Use targeted outreach for scarce experience.


As you[build a hiring pipeline](https://www.dover.com/blog/build-startup-hiring-pipeline) , keep job descriptions consistent across boards. Separate free distribution from paid advertising; spend where suitable candidates look.


Track candidate sources and outreach owners to compare channel quality and prevent duplicate contact.


## Step 4: Screen Applications and Build a Shortlist


Review applications against the role scorecard, then use an initial conversation to check qualifications and expectations about pay and scope.


Record a job-related reason for each decision:


-


Advance when evidence meets requirements.


-


Hold when a qualification needs clarification.


-


Decline when a required qualification is missing.


For first-time job seekers, count projects, coursework, internships, and transferable skills as evidence. If software or AI filters applications, keep human review and a reconsideration path for unclear experience. The[EEOC’s guidance on selection procedures](https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/employment-tests-and-selection-procedures) notes that employers remain responsible for confirming a screening tool is job-related, even when a vendor supplies it.


## Step 5: Conduct Structured Interviews and Assessments


Knowing[how to interview candidates for your startup](https://www.dover.com/blog/how-to-interview-candidates-for-your-startup) starts with giving each interview a distinct purpose; round counts depend on the role. An illustrative sequence:


-


Screening conversation: confirm mutual fit.


-


Role-focused assessment: ask about past decisions and use a realistic work sample tied to hiring-brief criteria.


-


Final discussion: resolve remaining evidence gaps.


Use consistent core questions and independent[interview scorecards](https://www.dover.com/blog/interview-scorecard-guide) before team discussion.[OPM’s structured interview guidance](https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/assessment-and-selection/structured-interviews/) describes asking every candidate the same predetermined questions and scoring answers on one rating scale. Share preparation guidance, time limits, and accommodation options beforehand. Keep assessments brief and accessible; avoid unpaid production work and repeated checks.


## Step 6: Make the Hiring Decision and Manage the Offer


As part of[full cycle recruiting](https://www.dover.com/blog/full-cycle-recruiting) , after interviews, collect feedback, debrief against evidence, resolve uncertainties, approve compensation, and communicate decisions. Plan references and background checks according to applicable consent and timing rules.


Send a written offer with contingencies, negotiate, record acceptance, and confirm the start date.


Adapt these emails:


> Employer: Sam will update you by Friday.


> Candidate: Sam, could you confirm next steps by Friday?


Notify unsuccessful applicants. If declined, reconsider qualified finalists or resume sourcing without lowering standards.


## Step 7: Complete Preboarding and Onboarding


This stage closes out[full life cycle recruiting](https://www.dover.com/blog/full-life-cycle-recruiting) : after acceptance, assign paperwork, equipment, and access setup. The hiring manager prepares role expectations, an initial work plan, and check-ins.


For U.S. hires, USCIS requires completion of Form I-9 Section 2 within[3 business days](https://www.uscis.gov/i-9-central/completing-form-i-9/completing-section-2-employer-review-and-attestation) of the first day of work for pay; if the job lasts less than 3 days, complete it no later than the first day of work for pay.


Keep legal deadlines separate from optional onboarding targets. Other locations need their own compliance checklist.


## A Simple Hiring Process Example for an Entry-Level Role


For a hypothetical junior customer support search, adapt the workflow template above: approve a funded role brief, write a job description that accepts relevant coursework, and use campus outreach to find candidates. Screen for transferable skills, then assess a sample ticket reply for accuracy and empathy.


After the candidate accepts a written offer, begin onboarding with product training and supervised replies. Explain assessment tasks and timing upfront.


## Hiring Process Metrics and Common Bottlenecks


Track Definition; response


Time to fill/hire Calendar days from requisition opening (fill) or the hired candidate’s pipeline entry (hire) to offer acceptance; inspect delays. See[Joveo’s metric definitions](https://www.joveo.com/blog/time-to-fill-vs-time-to-hire/) .


Time in stage Entry-to-exit days; reduce waits


Stage conversion Advanced/entered; revisit sourcing


Offer acceptance Accepted/issued; check misalignment


Recruiting cost Search spend/hires


Early outcomes Milestones at fixed tenure; review onboarding


Context SHRM 2026 Talent Trends:[68% report recruiting difficulty](https://www.shrm.org/about/press-room/shrm-unveils-2026-talent-trends-report--data-driven-insights-for) for full-time employees; not a startup benchmark


As part of a repeatable[recruiting process](https://www.dover.com/blog/recruiting-process-steps-hire-top-talent) , review completed searches for bottlenecks and outcomes, beyond speed.


## Tools and Ownership for a Repeatable Hiring Workflow


A spreadsheet and calendar may suffice for a small search. Consider a[free ATS for startups](https://www.dover.com/ats) when records, feedback, and handoffs scatter. Software tracks hiring process steps; people source, interview, assess, and close candidates.


-


Founder: approve exceptions.


-


Hiring manager: own selection decisions.


-


Interviewers: submit evidence.


-


Recruiting support or designated teammate: coordinate follow-ups.


Give each active candidate an owner and next action. Automation can assist with reminders, scheduling, and drafts; people remain responsible for decisions and candidate communication.


An ATS records stages, feedback, and next actions, but it does not source passive candidates, screen at volume, or close offers. For a few hires a year, a founder or hiring manager working inside the ATS can often cover those tasks. When several roles open at once, a role is senior or specialized, or no one has recruiting bandwidth, a fractional recruiter can take over sourcing, screening, or offer management inside the same ATS. The stage owners keep real-time visibility into the pipeline, and duplicate outreach is less likely.

## FAQs


### Can you shorten your hiring process steps when a role is urgent?


Yes, you can combine interviews that gather overlapping evidence, but keep budget approval, job-related assessment, and offer approval intact. Give each remaining interview a clear purpose, and agree on feedback deadlines before candidates enter the process.


### What’s a practical way to restart a paused search without starting over?


Reconfirm the role scope and budget before contacting previous candidates; an old shortlist may no longer match your needs. Review the available candidate records, check each person’s interest and availability, and collect fresh evidence only where requirements have changed.


### How do you move your hiring process from a spreadsheet into an ATS without losing track of candidates?


Clean up duplicate entries and give every active candidate a current stage, owner, and next action before moving records. Map your spreadsheet stages to the ATS’s interview plan, transfer the candidate records, and check that notes and pending follow-ups are accounted for before retiring the spreadsheet.


### Do I need a recruiter if I already use an ATS for these hiring process steps?


An ATS tracks candidates, feedback, and handoffs, but it does not source, screen, or close candidates on its own. Founders and hiring managers can often cover those tasks for occasional, well-defined roles. A recruiter becomes worth considering when several roles open together, a search is senior or specialized, or the hiring manager has little time. A fractional recruiter can work inside the same ATS, which gives the internal team and the recruiter one view of the pipeline. Dover pairs a free ATS with on-demand fractional recruiters in this way.


## Final Thoughts on Hiring From Approval to Onboarding


The seven stages of the hiring process connect budget approval to onboarding through a shared decision framework: each stage has an owner, an expected output, and criteria for moving forward. Clear handoffs between[hiring process steps](https://www.dover.com/) make it explicit who takes the next action, whether that means approving compensation or preparing a new hire’s first week. Time in stage, offer acceptance, and early hire outcomes can help distinguish delays from problems in selection or onboarding. A useful measure covers both how quickly a role closes and whether the new hire starts with the support needed to deliver the outcomes the role was created for. When stage owners run short on time, the decision usually comes down to hiring volume and role complexity: a self-serve ATS can carry a few well-defined hires, while a fractional recruiter working inside the same ATS adds capacity for concurrent or senior searches. Dover’s free ATS paired with on-demand fractional recruiters in one shared system is one example of that model.
